newsitem.title: UK: McDonald's resumes use of British beef.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's resumes use of British beef.

text.p: McDonald's Corp is to resume purchases of British beef for the burgers it sells in its 700 restaurants in the country, a company official said on Thursday.

McDonald's stopped buying British carcasses in March last year after scientists said there was a risk that the human brain condition Creutzfeldt Jakob Disease could be caught from eating meat from cows infected with "mad-cow disease".
Andrew Taylor, managing director of McDonald's British arm, said the company had conducted regular consumer opinion research to assess confidence in British beef.

"Recovery in confidence has been slow over the past year, but the results of our latest research, conducted this month, show that 74 percent of consumers now want us to sell British beef," Taylor said.
The company would begin buying British beef immediately and new supplies would start to be served in British McDonald's restaurants over the next few weeks.
